identification.summary: Storm-0381 is Microsoft's designation for a threat actor described as a Russian cybercrime group known for using malvertising to deploy Magniber ransomware [S2]. Its earlier Microsoft in-development designation was DEV-0381 [S2]. The Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2023 is the cited basis for this description [S2].
identification.notes: The Storm-0381 to Magniber link rests on a Malpedia entry that cites Microsoft's 2023 report; Microsoft's own wording was not opened [S2]. The Magniber malware family itself was first reported in 2017 [S3], but that is the malware, not necessarily this Microsoft-tracked cluster. Third-party Magniber reporting below does not name Storm-0381 and must not be merged with this actor without a primary Microsoft statement.

attribution.sponsor: Cybercrime (non-state), per Microsoft's description as relayed by Malpedia [S2]
attribution.confidence: Not stated in the sources reviewed
attribution.basis: Malpedia describes Storm-0381 as a Russian cybercrime group identified by Microsoft, citing the Digital Defense Report 2023 [S2]. No government attribution was found. No technical basis for the Russia assessment was available to this research.

objectives: Financial gain through ransomware deployment is implied by the description of the actor as a cybercrime group deploying Magniber ransomware [S2]. Magniber has been reported to demand ransoms of up to 2,500 USD from individuals in related third-party reporting, but that reporting was not retrieved with a citable date in this pass.

targeting.notes: Sources do not give Storm-0381-specific victimology. Magniber malware, as reported by third parties, initially targeted South Korea via malvertising [S3], with early variants checking for Korean system language [S3]. Google TAG reported in March 2023 that over 80 percent of downloads of malicious MSI files by users were in Europe, a departure from the usual Korea and Taiwan focus [S6]. Whether these map to Storm-0381 is unconfirmed.

capabilities.summary: Storm-0381 is described as using malvertising to deploy Magniber ransomware [S2]. Third-party reporting on Magniber, not confirmed as Storm-0381, shows: Magnitude Exploit Kit malvertising against Korean users in 2017 [S3]; signed APPX packages posing as Chrome or Edge updates in early 2022, which created a DLL and EXE under WindowsApps that downloaded and decoded the payload [S4]; and use of a SmartScreen bypass (malformed Authenticode signature) to evade warnings, patched as CVE-2022-44698 and then CVE-2023-24880 after a workaround variant [S6].

campaigns.name: Magniber via Magnitude Exploit Kit (malware family, actor link unconfirmed)
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reported Magnitude Exploit Kit malvertising delivering Magniber ransomware to South Korean users [S3]. Not attributed to Storm-0381 in the source.

campaigns.name: Fake Chrome and Edge update APPX distribution (actor link unconfirmed)
campaigns.summary: ASEC reported Magniber distributed through signed .appx packages disguised as Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome updates, shifting from Internet Explorer exploitation; the campaign was predominantly in South Korea [S4]. Not attributed to Storm-0381 in the sources.

campaigns.name: Magniber use of SmartScreen bypass variant (actor link unconfirmed)
campaigns.summary: Google TAG reported Magniber actors used a variant of a Microsoft SmartScreen bypass, patched as CVE-2023-24880 in the March 2023 Patch Tuesday release, after the earlier CVE-2022-44698 was fixed [S6]. Not attributed to Storm-0381 in the sources.

campaigns.name: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2023 listing
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's 2023 report is the cited origin of the Storm-0381 description as a Russian cybercrime group using malvertising to deploy Magniber [S2].

diamond.adversary: Russian cybercrime group per Microsoft's description relayed by Malpedia [S2].
diamond.capability: Malvertising delivery of Magniber ransomware [S2]; related Magniber reporting covers exploit kits, fake update lures and SmartScreen bypass [S3][S4][S6].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints and browsers (Chrome, Edge) and the Windows SmartScreen feature are the technologies abused in related Magniber reporting [S4][S6].

gaps: Microsoft's primary text on Storm-0381 (Digital Defense Report 2023) was not opened; its PDF URL was not confirmed in search and was removed.
No Microsoft blog or Defender TI profile for Storm-0381 was found; no named-actor (weather) promotion was found.
No evidence reviewed ties the Magniber campaigns in S3, S4 and S6 specifically to the Storm-0381 cluster; vendors (AhnLab, Google TAG, Trend Micro) do not use Microsoft's name.
Sponsor, confidence level, first-observed date, infrastructure, sector targeting and victim counts are unknown.
Not retrieved: HP Threat Research (JavaScript lure, Sept 2022), ASEC follow-up on cessation (Feb 2022), Picus CVE-2023-24880 write-up, Malpedia Magniber page.

provenance.importedSummary: Storm-0381 is a threat actor identified by Microsoft as a Russian cybercrime group. They are known for their use of malvertising to deploy Magniber, a type of ransomware.
